title: bug: JetBrains malformed-readiness loopback test intermittently times out
description: Full Windows Gradle test --rerun during task-048bfae2 hit TimeoutException at MoeProjectConnectionTest.kt:217 (malformed-readiness loop, .get(5, SECONDS)); 664 tests, 1 failure, 6 skipped. Log /tmp/tmp.fMm4SKyBQc; exact unchanged rerun /tmp/tmp.wv4xH0vpx8 passed 664/0 failures. Investigate loopback/pending-readiness race or timing without weakening malformed-response assertions.
definitionOfDone: Reproduce or instrument the intermittent malformed-readiness timeout and document its root cause.
Add a deterministic regression test for any corrected production/test synchronization and pass the focused connection class and full JetBrains suite under jetbrains-gradle.

implementationPlan.description:
DoD 1: reproduce the flake and record its root cause. There is no repo change in this step and no Gradle run, so no lease is needed. The architect already reproduced it outside the plugin with a standalone Java harness against the same Java-WebSocket 1.6.0 jar: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/plan-8784d35d/harness/ (README.md holds the exact commands; SHA256SUMS sits one level up). Re-run it with the Windows JDK 17 from WSL. Compile, then run:
- `ReadinessStress 9 1500 5000` (9 round trips per fresh connection, like the malformed test) at least 3 times;
- `ReadinessStress 9 1500 5000 rearm` at least 3 times;
- `StrandCheck 200` once.

Expected, from the architect's runs:
- Without rearm, about 1 timeout per 6,600 round trips (11 in 72,900). Every TIMEOUT line shows serverReceived == serverSent == expected, serverOutQueue=1 and serverInterestOps=1 (OP_READ only), and one extra onWriteDemand delivers the stranded reply within 1 s.
- With rearm, 0 timeouts (0 in 81,000).
- StrandCheck: 0 leaked and 0 undelivered of 200.

The root cause to record (it also goes into the fixture KDoc in step 2): the loopback daemon in MoeProjectConnectionTest is Java-WebSocket's WebSocketServer, which can leave a sent frame queued while the connection's selection key is back on OP_READ. Here is how, verified with javap on the 1.6.0 jar:
- WebSocketImpl.write does outQueue.put, then WebSocketServer.onWriteDemand sets interestOps(5) and calls wakeup.
- The selector's doWrite runs SocketChannelIOHelper.batch, and when that drains the queue it sets interestOps(1).
- Nothing orders the two, so the frame waits for the next write demand on that connection.

The fixture writes nothing but its answers, so a stranded answer never left, and `requestExecutionReadiness().get(5, SECONDS)` at MoeProjectConnectionTest.kt:217 threw TimeoutException. The malformed test is the one that hit it because it makes 9 round trips (about 1% per run). Production is not exposed: the plugin's server is the Node daemon, and its Java-WebSocket client writes from a dedicated thread off a blocking queue. Write these numbers into complete_task's summary. If your runs disagree with the architect's, stop and record that with moe.add_comment before step 2.
implementationPlan.note: Recompiled checksum-verified standalone harness with Windows JDK 17. Baseline 3x13,500: 3/0/2 timeouts (5/40,500); each stalled with received=sent=expected, outQueue=1, interestOps=1; extra demand delivered all five. Rearm 3x13,500: 0/40,500 timeouts. StrandCheck 200: zero leaks, zero undelivered. Confirms selector doWrite OP_READ reset races send's OP_READ|OP_WRITE update; plugin future registration/parser correct. Quality gate parity + lint also freshly passed. No repository changes.

implementationPlan.description:
DoD 2: the fixture fix plus two deterministic regression tests, all in moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin/com/moe/services/MoeProjectConnectionTest.kt, and no other file. Make the file byte-identical to /mnt/d/moe-scratch/plan-8784d35d/ref/MoeProjectConnectionTest.expected.kt (sha256 ad611f518693450f283f29ca9ecb3f09c0d42047a731778a05077a5326b11978). It is uncompiled, because an architect seat cannot hold the jetbrains-gradle lease (mem:gotcha-architect-cannot-take-gradle-lease). Apply it with your own editor tool only (Edit on Claude, apply_patch on codex exec), never a shell copy (project rail). The file is LF.

The diff:
(a) Add `import org.java_websocket.WebSocketImpl`.
(b) In ConnectionFixture:
- a `@Volatile var enqueue: (WebSocket, String) -> Unit = { conn, text -> conn.send(text) }`;
- the server's onMessage still records every frame, and on an answer runs `this@ConnectionFixture.enqueue(socket, answer)` and then `this@ConnectionFixture.flush(socket)`;
- `serverConnection()` returns `server.connections.single()`;
- `flush(conn): Boolean` calls server.onWriteDemand(conn) and Thread.sleep(1) until `(conn as WebSocketImpl).outQueue` is empty, for at most 2 s, and returns whether it drained. Its KDoc is the root-cause record;
- `strand(conn, text)` puts `impl.draft.createFrames(text, false)` through `impl.draft.createBinaryFrame` onto `impl.outQueue` with no write demand. That is exactly the stuck state the flake leaves.
Every library member used here is public in 1.6.0 (javap): WebSocketImpl.outQueue, getDraft(), Draft.createFrames(String, boolean), createBinaryFrame(Framedata) and WebSocketServer.onWriteDemand(WebSocket).
(c) Two new tests after the malformed one, on new pids 41019 and 41020:
- 'a frame queued without a write demand stays unsent until flush re-arms it' requests readiness with no automatic answer and waits for the GET_EXECUTION_READINESS frame. It strands a valid EXECUTION_READINESS and asserts the future is NOT done after 300 ms. That control proves the stuck state is real. It then asserts flush(conn) returns true and the future is Answered(ExecutionReadiness("verified-local", true, [], null)).
- 'a reply the loopback server strands still answers the request' sets `fixture.enqueue = fixture::strand`, answers readiness, and asserts the same Answered value from get(5, SECONDS). That proves onMessage's flush wiring.
The architect checked both premises with StrandCheck: 200 of 200. They are deterministic, because nothing else writes on that connection and the libraries' 60 s ping timers never fire inside a test.

The malformed test and every other assertion stay untouched; do not weaken them (task rule). Error handling: flush is bounded at 2 s and returns false rather than hanging, so the waiting request then fails at its own timeout with a clear message, under the class's 30 s Timeout rule. An InterruptedException from Thread.sleep can only happen during server.stop teardown, where the library routes it to the fixture's empty onError.

Run the focused test class under the jetbrains-gradle lease (mem:convention-jetbrains-gradle-lease; acquire it, and release it after every run, even a failed one). WSL has no JDK (mem:gotcha-jetbrains-gradle-from-wsl). From the worktree root: `cmd.exe /d /c "set GRADLE_OPTS=-Xmx512m&& cd /d $(wslpath -w "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)") && moe-jetbrains\gradlew.bat -p moe-jetbrains test --tests com.moe.services.MoeProjectConnectionTest --rerun"`. Expected: tests=16 failures=0. On a compile error, read the FIRST e: line.

implementationPlan.description:
Adversarial self-review of THIS task's diff: load adversarial-self-review. The epic is a rolling bucket and isEpicFinal comes from the highest-order fallback, so the review covers this task. Step 3's full plugin suite is the regression gate. Only one test file changes, and no production code.

Run the mutants under the jetbrains-gradle lease in a copy outside the checkout, never in the worktree (mem:gotcha-jetbrains-qa-mutants-in-archive-copy, worker variant): `git archive HEAD moe-jetbrains | tar -x -C /mnt/d/moe-scratch/m-8784`, then cp --parents your changed file. Run `--tests com.moe.services.MoeProjectConnectionTest --rerun` once per mutant, restore the file, and cmp it at the end.
- M1: drop `server.onWriteDemand(conn)` from flush. Both new tests must fail: flush returns false, and the wiring test's get(5, SECONDS) times out.
- M2: drop the `flush(socket)` call from onMessage. 'a reply the loopback server strands still answers the request' must fail.
- M3: make strand call `conn.send(text)`. The control assertion 'A stranded frame must not leave on its own' must fail.

Also check by reading:
- flush runs on the server's single worker thread, so a 1 ms sleep only delays the next frame's processing.
- flush's duplicate onWriteDemand calls are harmless: they re-set the same interest and wake the selector.
- `server.connections.single()` holds because each fixture opens one connection per test.
- No other assertion in the class changed.

Out of scope, so do not touch it: MoeSnapshotProjectCheckTest also sends from its loopback server's onOpen, but 3,000 such greetings stranded none (OpenStress), so it gets no change here. Record the mutant results and the harness numbers in complete_task's summary.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: MoeProjectConnectionTest's loopback server re-arms its write demand after every answer until the frame has left. A reply stranded by Java-WebSocket 1.6.0's server write-interest race is therefore still delivered, and the malformed-readiness loop no longer times out. Two deterministic tests reproduce the stranded state and prove the flush and its wiring. Production code is unchanged.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: 1) A production change in MoeProjectService (retry, or correlate readiness replies): rejected. The plugin registers the future before sending and completes it on any reply, and the stall is in the test's Java server, which production never uses. 2) Raising the test's 5 s wait: rejected. A stranded frame waits for the next write demand (up to the 60 s ping), so a longer wait only hides it. 3) Upgrading Java-WebSocket: 1.6.0 is the version the plugin ships, and a library bump would touch production's client. 4) A periodic pump re-arming every connection: rejected for a send-local flush, which runs only when the fixture writes and is bounded. 5) A fixture test that loops thousands of round trips: rejected as nondeterministic. The two tests construct the stranded state directly (strand) and prove both the flush and its wiring.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: MoeProjectService.requestExecutionReadiness registers the future in pendingReadiness before sending GET_EXECUTION_READINESS, and completeReadiness completes every waiter on any EXECUTION_READINESS (there is no correlation id). The dispatcher's EXECUTION_READINESS branch never throws: it maps a non-object payload to MALFORMED. The test fixture's WebSocketServer(addr, 1) uses one decoder thread, and onMessage runs there. Java-WebSocket 1.6.0's WebSocketImpl.outQueue and the Draft frame builders are public. The class has a 30 s Timeout rule and bounded closeWithin (task-ba9590ce).
planningNotes.risks: The reference bytes are uncompiled: on a compile failure, read the first e: line. The control assertion relies on nothing else writing on the connection within 300 ms: the fixture's answers are off (reply returns null), and the libraries' connection-lost pings start 60 s after open. The harness numbers vary run to run; the no-rearm rate was about 1 per 6,600 round trips, so a single 13,500-round run can show 0.
